original_question: Assume that in dimension d+1 the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket is trivial, meaning the flow Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) can be written as the Schouten bracket [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]] for some vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}. Determine whether that trivializing vector field can always be constructed as a linear combination of descendants, in dimension d+1, of the two-dimensional 'sunflower' graph.
target_in_paper: Section 2, first bullet in the unnumbered list of open problems immediately after Proposition 1: “If dot P = Q_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) is trivial, Q_{γ3}^{d+1} = [[P, X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]], then is X_{γ3}^{d+1} found over linear combinations of the ‘sunflower’ descendants from 2D?” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact conditional structure and the exact object of the paper’s first open problem: it is about the tetrahedral γ3-flow in dimension d+1, assumes Poisson-triviality in the form Q_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]], and asks whether the trivializing 1-vector can be sought among linear combinations of descendants of the 2D sunflower. That is essentially the paper’s wording. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
missing_details: The ambient class should be stated more narrowly: P is not an arbitrary Nambu-Poisson bracket, but the Nambu-determinant Poisson bivector on the affine real space R^{d+1} coming from Eq. (1), with coefficient ϱ(x) and Casimirs a_1,...,a_{d-1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The quantifier should be explicit: the question is dimension-by-dimension, for each fixed d+1 >= 3 (equivalently d >= 2), under the assumption that the tetrahedral flow is trivial in that dimension. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
The 2D sunflower should be identified explicitly as the graph X_{γ3}^{d=2} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The word “descendants” should be defined using Section 2: when passing from d to d+1, one attaches the new Casimir to each Levi-Civita vertex and expands, via Leibniz rule, each external arrow that originally hits a Casimir; this is narrower than arbitrary lifts or embeddings. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

It helps to say that the search space is an R-linear combination of Nambu micro-graphs, matching the paper’s graph-combinatorial setup on affine real manifolds. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The degree data are implicit in the paper and should be made stand-alone: Q_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) is quartic in P, while X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3}) is a cubic 1-vector. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The ambient deformation-theoretic assumption that P is Poisson, hence lies in the Nambu subset of Poisson brackets, is tacit in the draft and should be made explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The paper asks for existence of some trivializer within that ansatz, not uniqueness and not the stronger second-bullet claim involving the union of descendants of X_{γ3}^d with vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs over R^d. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
refined_question: For each fixed d >= 2, let P be the Nambu-determinant Poisson bivector on the affine space R^{d+1}, defined by {f,g}_{d+1}(x) = ϱ(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-1})/∂(x^1,...,x^{d+1})). Assume that the tetrahedral Kontsevich γ3-flow on this Nambu class is Poisson-trivial in dimension d+1, i.e. there exists a cubic 1-vector X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3}) such that Q_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]]. Must one then be able to choose X_{γ3}^{d+1} as an R-linear combination of the (iterated) (d+1)-dimensional Nambu micro-graph descendants of the two-dimensional sunflower graph X_{γ3}^{d=2} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2), where “descendants” are understood in the sense of Section 2 via adjoining the new Casimir and expanding the relevant arrows by Leibniz rule? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
justification: The draft is targeting the first open problem in Section 2 almost verbatim, not a neighboring statement. The necessary paper-specific context comes from Eq. (1), which fixes the Nambu-determinant brackets on R^d; footnote 5, which defines the 2D sunflower; and the Section 2 definition of descendants. Proposition 1 is nearby context showing why descendant-based ansätze matter: in dimension 4, no new vanishing 1-vectors appear outside descendants of vanishing 3D descendants of the sunflower. Because your draft does not mention adjoining vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs or the union with descendants of the lower-dimensional solution, it should be aligned with the first bullet only, not with the stronger second bullet. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
